clue.text: Report of anything but feebleness in small child

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word meaning strength is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the opposite of feebleness is might, i.e. strength

explanation.surface: Someone describes a little child as anything but feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report of' signals a sound-alike: MIGHT, the opposite of feebleness, is said aloud and entered as MITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is an affectionate word for a tiny youngster, as in 'poor little mite'.

clue.text: Bird quietly gets something on allotment, nipping head off

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: the head of the vegetable is nipped off, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a carrot is a vegetable grown on an allotment

explanation.surface: A bird quietly snips the top off something growing in a vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot of land where British people grow vegetables; the indicator 'nipping head off' removes just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a familiar kind of bird, often kept as a talking pet.

clue.text: God of war hurries, leader going out

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for hurries departs

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, so hares means hurries

explanation.surface: The god of war rushes off while his commander leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader going out' drops the first letter H from HARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek deity of battle, counterpart of the Roman Mars.

clue.text: Complained, being given drink that's hard to swallow

indicators.note: the word for being served drink takes in the letter for hard

parts.note: to be wined is to be served wine
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone moaned about a drink that was difficult to get down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To swallow' puts H inside WINED. 'Hard to swallow' looks like a phrase about the drink, but 'hard' is the letter and 'to swallow' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To whine is to grumble in a high plaintive voice, so whined is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Italian painter is in Paris, being bolder than anyone else

parts.note: Filippo Lippi (or his son Filippino) was an Italian Renaissance painter
est is French for is

explanation.surface: An Italian artist turns up in Paris, more daring than everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lippy is informal for cheeky or impudent, so the superlative means the most brazen of all.

clue.text: Notice embassies making entrance charges

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
diplomatic missions are embassies

explanation.surface: A notice says embassies are charging for entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissions are the fees paid to get into a venue, as in admission prices.

clue.text: Optimist in trouble, I beam and crow — nothing to lose

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disorder, so they are rearranged
the jumble must shed the letter for nothing, leaving the answer

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A hopeful person in difficulty smiles and boasts, having nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' rearranges IBEAMCROW; 'to lose' then removes one O. Mr Micawber, of Dickens's David Copperfield, is ever sure 'something will turn up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkins Micawber is the archetype of hopeful improvidence, so his name stands for any incurable optimist.

clue.text: Attack dull lot of people going in the wrong direction

indicators.note: in a down clue the words run backwards, read from the end

parts.note: drab means dull
a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: A boring crowd launches an assault but heads the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going in the wrong direction' turns DRABMOB round.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard is to assail continuously, originally with artillery fire.

clue.text: Bob maybe has house across two roads

indicators.note: the house abbreviation stretches across the road letters, holding them inside

parts.note: AI (the A1, Britain's longest numbered road) and RD, short for road

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob owns a house spanning two roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the haircut. The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh, written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short, straight-cut hairstyle, an example of a hairdo, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Nasty headache puts Margaret on edge

parts.note: Meg is a short form of Margaret
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A dreadful headache leaves Margaret on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Megrim is an old word for migraine, a severe one-sided headache.

clue.text: Maybe Mark's sorting out secs and typing pool

indicators.note: the letters are sorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps called Mark, organises the secretaries and the typing pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' seems to be an office manager; he is the evangelist. 'Secs' looks like seconds or secretaries; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark's account is one of the three similar New Testament books, with Matthew and Luke, so it is an example.

clue.text: Not the quality of a 'Dexter-type' writer!

definitions.text: Not the quality of a 'Dexter-type' writer!

parts.words: Not the quality of a 'Dexter-type' writer!
parts.note: dexter is Latin for right, so a dexter-type writer uses the right hand; the quality wanted is the opposite

explanation.surface: A reviewer complains a novelist lacks the class of Colin Dexter, the Inspector Morse author.
explanation.walkthrough: Dexter looks like the crime novelist Colin Dexter; read it as Latin dexter, right-handed, from which 'dexterous' comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring the left hand is the opposite of the right-handedness implied by dexter.

clue.text: Finally the bully arrives to restrict disorder briefly produced by aggressive Green?

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word the is used

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully them

indicators.note: the arrival abbreviation hems in the shortened disorder word

parts.note: ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

indicators.note: the word is cut short by one letter at its end

parts.note: a riot is public disorder

explanation.surface: A bully finally arrives to quell trouble caused by a combative environmentalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' is a verb here, not a person. The shortened disorder word sits between the two Rs of the timetable abbreviation, which 'to restrict' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-warrior is a militant environmental campaigner, a Green who takes direct action.

clue.text: Eccentric character turning up to entertain one, a famous physicist

indicators.note: the reversed word takes in the letter for one as a guest
in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a card is an amusing oddball
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An odd character turns up to amuse someone, namely a renowned scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' makes DRAC from CARD, and 'to entertain' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac was the British Nobel laureate who founded much of quantum mechanics and predicted antimatter.

clue.text: I really dislike that book — it's an embarrassment

parts.note: boo is the jeer of someone expressing disapproval

explanation.surface: A reader declares a book they hate to be a disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a blunder, the kind of gaffe that causes red faces.

clue.text: Dances around American street where folk may be waiting

indicators.note: the dancing word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to bop is to dance

explanation.surface: People dance around an American street while others wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Bus stops are the roadside places where passengers queue for the next bus.

clue.text: Number deserting beach, coming back for indoor game

indicators.note: the remaining letters are read in reverse
the number letter leaves the beach word

parts.note: a strand is a shore or beach

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the beach and comes home for a pub game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserting' takes N from STRAND, leaving STRAD; 'coming back' turns it round. 'Number' looks like a crowd; it is the letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is the pub game of throwing small missiles at a board, played indoors.

clue.text: Yorkshire town rubbish collector taking a certain weight

parts.note: a skip is a large open container for builders' rubbish
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: In a northern town a binman takes on a particular load.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip, in Britain, is a big metal bin left on the street for waste. 'Rubbish collector' looks like a binman.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipton is a market town in North Yorkshire, the 'gateway to the Dales'.

clue.text: Old-fashioned trust finally went with quarrel

indicators.note: the last letter only of the following word is taken

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Faith in old ways eventually ended in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to follow 'trust'; it applies to 'went', giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Trow is an archaic verb meaning to believe or trust, as in 'I trow'.

clue.text: Is it Bacon's art form ultimately? It's somewhat different

definitions.text: Is it Bacon's art form ultimately? It's somewhat different

indicators.note: the letters are made different, i.e. rearranged into a new order
only the last letter of the word form is used

explanation.surface: A critic wonders whether Francis Bacon's painting is ultimately this movement, though rather unlike it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: Bacon's figurative painting is somewhat different from pure abstraction. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstractionism is non-representational art, a mode the distorted figures of painter Francis Bacon resemble but differ from.

clue.text: Boy that's amiss edges away, bad lad

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word for amiss are taken away

parts.note: amiss means wrong

indicators.note: bad signals the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy has gone astray: he is a naughty lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges away' strips WRONG to RON; 'bad' rearranges LAD as ALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald is a male first name, so it can stand for any boy in crosswords.

clue.text: Disciple turned up outside a church offering chips

indicators.note: the reversed disciple word sits outside the other letters
in a down clue the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a son can mean a follower or disciple, as in a son of the Church

explanation.surface: A follower turns up outside a church selling snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' gives NOS; 'outside' wraps it round ACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Nachos are Mexican tortilla crisps, usually served with melted cheese and toppings.

clue.text: Material on northern island's buried

indicators.note: the two pieces are buried within the island name

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island; the 's is is, linking it to the indicator

explanation.surface: Some fabric on a northern island has been buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretonne is a heavy printed cotton fabric used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Native of northern land in modest home

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A northerner lives in a humble house.
explanation.definitionFit: Esth is an old word for an Estonian, someone from the Baltic country.

clue.text: Watch determined person losing head and heart

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a sticker is someone who sticks at things

explanation.surface: Watch out: a stubborn person may lose their head and their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer has two definitions, 'Watch' and 'heart', both slang senses, either side of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for both a clock-like timepiece and the beating organ in the chest.

clue.text: Make something for the traditional tea lady, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the vessel is taken by its sound

parts.words: something for the traditional tea lady
parts.note: a tea lady pouring from an urn, the large heated vessel

explanation.surface: Someone produces something for the old-style office tea lady.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea lady was a woman who wheeled a trolley round British offices serving tea from an urn. 'We hear' turns URN into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to make money, as in making a living.

clue.text: See 11
It may be mis-served to a diner with love for what's English

definitions.text: It may be mis-served to a diner with love for what's English

indicators.note: the dish is served wrongly, its letters jumbled
the letter for love stands in place of the letter for English

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A curry might be served to a customer wrongly, as a loving stand-in for English food.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing the E of TOADINER to O gives TOADINOR, which 'mis-served' rearranges. The whole clue describes the curry too.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori is Indian food baked in a clay oven, a dish restaurants serve diners.
